F. Significant Effects on Groundwater, Flood Plains, Wetlands and Coastal Zones.
Every effort has been made to avoid implicating any water supply source, treatment or distribution system.
In the improvement of this highway, present drainage patterns will be maintained. Erosion and sedimentation due to roadway drainage will be minimized by seeding or sodding of exposed earth surfaces.
The improvement should not adversely disturb the ecological balance of the surrounding land or water. Since the improvement for the most part will utilize the existing roadway, there should be no significant effect upon the surrounding land or water areas caused by the proposed improvement.
The improvement should not alter the pattern of behavior for any known genus or species.
There are no important breeding, nesting or feeding grounds in the area of the improvement.
The improvement will be generally on the existing alignment with little change in the highway gradient. Therefore, the water table of the area will not be adversely affected.
Drainage for this improvement is in accordance with the provisions and limitations established by the General Assembly of the State of Illinois, as contained in the Illinois Revised Statutes.
Based upon the enactment of legislation, the use of highway funds for other than highway purposes is restricted. Highway drainage is designed to prevent the accumulation and retention of water on and by the highway. Also, in accordance with the State Laws governing the expenditure of highway funds, improvements to the drainage of areas outside of the right-of-way are not considered unless the highway will benefit thereby. Highway right-of-way does nothing to change the natural system of drainage or increase the flow to the downstream channel that the channel is not required to accept by State law. (See Appendix E.)
